prompt.context_jp: 真藤だけ___、驚いたように舞を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 真藤だけ___、驚いたように舞を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 'Shindō alone'.

feedback.correct_en: '〜だけが' marks exhaustive listing — only Shindō (and no one else) was staring at Mai. が goes with this exclusive/identifying nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜だけは would mean 'at least Shindō' or contrast him with others on a different predicate, which doesn't fit here.

prompt.context_jp: 芹澤の表情だけ___、彫像のように動かなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 芹澤の表情だけ___、彫像のように動かなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after '芹澤の表情だけ'.

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: everyone else reacted, but Serizawa's expression alone did NOT move. 〜だけは highlights contrast with the surrounding reactions.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけが would exhaustively identify ('only his expression moved'), the opposite of the intended contrast with the stunned executives.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼だけは笑わなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 舞___膝の上で拳を握り、真藤の横顔を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞___膝の上で拳を握り、真藤の横顔を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'Mai clenched her fists...'

feedback.correct_en: Mai is the ongoing protagonist/topic of the scene — は marks her as the established theme for the narrative.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Mai as newly-introduced information, which clashes with her being the viewpoint character throughout.

prompt.context_jp: 荒木の額___は、じわりと汗が浮かび始めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 荒木の額___、じわりと汗が浮かび始めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: '___ Araki's forehead, sweat began to form.'

feedback.correct_en: 浮かぶ (appear/form) takes に to mark the location where something comes into existence — 'ON his forehead.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks a location where an action happens actively; passive appearance/existence takes に. を doesn't fit this intransitive verb.

prompt.context_jp: しかし芹澤___、荒木のほうを見ようともしなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかし芹澤___、荒木のほうを見ようともしなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'But Serizawa...did not even look.'

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は with しかし: Araki looked to Serizawa for help, but Serizawa, in contrast, didn't even return the glance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Serizawa as new information, missing the explicit contrast set up by しかし.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は来たが、私は行かない。
contrast_examples.en: He came, but I'm not going (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: こんなことができるのは この銀行に ただ1人しかいません 芹澤頭取 あなた___。
prompt.prompt_jp: こんなことができるのは、この銀行にただ1人しかいません。芹澤頭取、あなた___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'It's YOU, President Serizawa.'

feedback.correct_en: The exhaustive identification 'the one who can do this is YOU' is completed with です — identifying Serizawa as the sole possible agent.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'you' a topic awaiting a comment, and が alone leaves the clause incomplete here.

prompt.context_jp: 不祥事を起こしたの___、芹澤頭取、あなたです！
prompt.prompt_jp: 不祥事を起こしたの___、芹澤頭取、あなたです！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'The one who caused the scandal is you, President Serizawa!'

feedback.correct_en: 〜のは〜だ cleft construction: 'As for who caused the scandal, it's you.' The nominalized clause takes は, and the identified answer follows.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would be ungrammatical in this cleft frame; the pattern 〜のは…だ requires は on the nominalized subject.

contrast_examples.en: The one who broke it is him.

prompt.context_jp: ここで働く人たち___、銀行員である前に、ひとりの人間です。
prompt.prompt_jp: ここで働く人たち___、銀行員である前に、ひとりの人間です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the people who work here'.

feedback.correct_en: General statement/definition about a topic: 'As for the people who work here, they are human beings first.' は sets up a categorical claim.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark them as newly identified subjects, incompatible with the generic/definitional statement Mai is making.

prompt.context_jp: みんな、何か言うこと___ないのか？
prompt.prompt_jp: みんな、何か言うこと___ないのか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'Doesn't anyone have anything to say?'

feedback.correct_en: With ある/ない in rhetorical/emphatic questioning, 〜ことはないのか marks 'anything to say' as the topic being challenged.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be a neutral 'is there anything,' losing Serizawa's confrontational emphasis. を is wrong because ある/ない don't take direct objects.

prompt.context_jp: 全ては… 芹澤頭取の指示___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 全ては… 芹澤頭取の指示___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the ending that identifies the source of all this.

feedback.correct_en: '全ては…指示でした' — identifying copula clause. 全ては (topic) + Xでした (identification).
feedback.incorrect_en: がした doesn't fit a noun identification; the structure needs the copula to equate 'everything' with 'president's orders.'

contrast_examples.jp: 原因は彼の指示でした。

prompt.context_jp: やがて、テーブルの一角から一人の男___静かに立ち上がった。
prompt.prompt_jp: やがて、テーブルの一角から一人の男___静かに立ち上がった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'A man stood up quietly.'

feedback.correct_en: '一人の男' is being newly introduced to the scene — new information/entity, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require this man to be a known topic, but he's just now entering the narrative spotlight.

prompt.context_jp: いつの間にか、舞の背後___父の幸三が立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: いつの間にか、舞の背後___父の幸三が立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'behind Mai, her father was standing.'

feedback.correct_en: 立っている expresses a state of existence at a location; に marks the location of being/existing.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks locations of active actions; the stative '(someone) is standing there' takes に.

contrast_examples.en: There are people at the station (existence).

prompt.context_jp: 会議室は___ように静まり返った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会議室は___ように静まり返った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom: 'The room fell silent as if...'

feedback.correct_en: 水を打ったように is a set simile meaning 'as if sprinkled with water' — i.e. instantly, completely silent. Standard collocation with 静まり返る.
feedback.incorrect_en: 火を見たよう ('clear as seeing fire') means 'obvious,' and 油を注ぐ ('pour oil') means to inflame — neither describes sudden silence.

contrast_examples.jp: 水を打ったような静けさ

prompt.context_jp: 舞は、___に切り込む覚悟を決めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞は、___に切り込む覚悟を決めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression: 'resolved to cut in ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 単刀直入 (literally 'single sword, direct entry') means 'getting straight to the point' — exactly what Mai is about to do with Serizawa.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一刀両断 means 'cutting decisively in two' (making a bold judgment), and 二束三文 means 'dirt cheap.' Neither fits 'confronting directly.'

prompt.context_jp: 「___ようですが… 不祥事を起こしたのは、芹澤頭取、あなたです！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ようですが… 不祥事を起こしたのは、芹澤頭取、あなたです！」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the polite preface Mai uses before contradicting the president.

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返すようですが is a polite set phrase for 'I hate to contradict you, but...' — exactly Mai's stance toward Serizawa.
feedback.incorrect_en: お言葉に甘える means 'to take you up on your offer,' and お手を煩わせる means 'to trouble you.' Neither prefaces disagreement.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが、違います。
contrast_examples.en: Forgive me for contradicting, but no.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉に甘えて、頂きます。
contrast_examples.en: I'll take you up on your kind offer.

prompt.context_jp: だから、___ 一生懸命 働いてるんです！
prompt.prompt_jp: だから、___一生懸命 働いてるんです！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'gritting their teeth.'

feedback.correct_en: 歯を食いしばる ('clench one's teeth') is the idiomatic expression for enduring hardship while persisting — fits 'working hard despite everything.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 口をとがらせる means 'to pout' and 首をかしげる means 'to tilt one's head (in doubt)' — neither conveys endurance.

contrast_examples.jp: 歯を食いしばって耐える。

prompt.context_jp: この数日、二人は足を___して都内を歩き回った。
prompt.prompt_jp: この数日、二人は足を___して都内を歩き回った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word completing 'walked around until legs were ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 足を棒にする ('make one's legs into sticks') is a set idiom for walking so much your legs feel stiff/exhausted.
feedback.incorrect_en: 山に and 板に are not idiomatic with 足. Only 棒 completes this fixed expression.

contrast_examples.en: To get the hang of (unrelated idiom).

prompt.context_jp: 時計の秒針の音さえ聞こえそうな静けさの中で、誰も___一つしない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の秒針の音さえ聞こえそうな静けさの中で、誰も___一つしない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun: 'no one made a single ___.'

feedback.correct_en: 身じろぎ means 'slight movement/stir.' 身じろぎ一つしない = 'doesn't stir even slightly' — the standard phrase for frozen stillness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 身支度 means 'getting dressed/preparing,' and 身の上 means 'one's circumstances.' Neither fits the context of silent stillness.

prompt.context_jp: その顔から、みるみるうちに___が引いていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その顔から、みるみるうちに___が引いていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word: 'the ___ drained from his face.'

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く ('the blood drains') is the standard idiom for turning pale from shock or fear — matches Serizawa's realization.
feedback.incorrect_en: 眠気 (sleepiness) and やる気 (motivation) can 'leave' but don't collocate with 顔から〜引く to describe going pale.

prompt.context_jp: 一介の女子行員が役員会で___など、この銀行では前代未聞のことだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一介の女子行員が役員会で___など、この銀行では前代未聞のことだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose: 'for a mere employee to ___ at a board meeting.'

feedback.correct_en: 声を上げる means to 'raise one's voice'/'speak out' publicly or in protest — exactly what Mai does by interrupting.
feedback.incorrect_en: 声をかける is 'to call out/address someone' (casual), and 声を潜める is 'to lower one's voice' — the opposite.

prompt.context_jp: Mai is passionately refuting Serizawa in the boardroom.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as Mai's impassioned retort?

choices.text: 手柄は上司のもの、ミスは部下のもの、そんな常識この銀行でしか通用しません！
手柄が上司のもので、ミスが部下のもので、そんな常識この銀行でしか通用しません！

feedback.correct_en: The parallel contrastive は structure (手柄は…ミスは…) creates the rhetorical balance that makes the statement punchy and natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using が and connecting with で flattens the contrast into a bland description, losing the oratorical rhythm Mai needs.

contrast_examples.en: Work by day, rest by night (parallel contrast).

contrast_examples.jp: 昼が働きで夜が休みで…

prompt.context_jp: Shindo is finally defying Serizawa.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for 'if it collapses, so be it'?

choices.text: もしそれでつぶれてしまうのであれば、こんな腐った銀行、つぶれるべきです！
もしそれでつぶれてしまうのであれば、こんな腐った銀行、つぶれなければなりません！

feedback.correct_en: つぶれるべきです ('ought to collapse') conveys moral judgment appropriate here. The 〜べき carries the normative weight Shindo intends.
feedback.incorrect_en: つぶれなければなりません means 'must collapse' as an obligation/necessity, which sounds odd — a bank doesn't have a duty to collapse.

contrast_examples.jp: 悪は滅びなければならない。

prompt.context_jp: Araki is denying everything indignantly.
prompt.prompt_en: Which denial sounds more natural coming from a cornered senior employee?

choices.text: 1億なんて知らない。白水銀行になど行くはずがないだろう。
1億なんて知らないです。白水銀行に行かないと思います。

feedback.correct_en: The blunt plain-form denial with 〜はずがないだろう fits Araki's agitated, defensive outburst at a subordinate's accusation.
feedback.incorrect_en: The polite/hedged version (〜ないと思います) sounds timid and uncertain — a cornered executive wouldn't downplay his denial this way.

contrast_examples.jp: 行くはずがないだろう。

prompt.context_jp: Opening a formal emergency board meeting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which opening sounds most natural for a board meeting chair?

choices.text: それでは、臨時役員会を始めさせていただきます。
それじゃ、臨時役員会を始めるね。

feedback.correct_en: 始めさせていただきます is the standard humble-polite opening for formal corporate meetings — matches the gravity of the setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: 始めるね with それじゃ is casual spoken Japanese inappropriate for addressing a boardroom of executives.

contrast_examples.jp: 会議を始めさせていただきます。
contrast_examples.en: We shall now begin the meeting (formal).

prompt.context_jp: Mai scrapes the paint and reveals the gold.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural at the dramatic reveal?

feedback.correct_en: これは純金です presents 'this' as the known item and 純金 as the revealed new information — the natural reveal order.
feedback.incorrect_en: 純金はこれです ('as for pure gold, it's this one') presupposes pure gold is the topic being searched for, which doesn't match the surprise moment.

contrast_examples.en: The real one is this (answer to a search).
